name: Karnataka GK
description: Karnataka-specific general knowledge: culture, economy, people and state facts.

questions.question: Karnataka Rajyotsava (state formation day) is celebrated on which date?
questions.explanation: The state was formed as Mysore State on 1 November 1956 and renamed Karnataka on 1 November 1973 — both are commemorated on Rajyotsava.

questions.question: How many districts does Karnataka have as of 2024?
questions.explanation: Karnataka has 31 districts, the newest being Vijayanagara (carved out of Ballari in 2020).

questions.question: What is the state animal of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The Asian Elephant is Karnataka's state animal; sandalwood is the state tree and the Indian roller (Neelakantha) the state bird.

questions.question: D. R. Bendre, the 'Varakavi' (poet of the boon) of Kannada literature, won the Jnanpith for which poetry collection?
questions.explanation: Bendre's 'Nakutanti' (1964) won the Jnanpith (1974). Kuvempu's 'Sri Ramayana Darshanam' won it first, in 1967.

questions.question: The Kadambas, founded by Mayurasharma with Banavasi as capital, are historically significant as what?
questions.explanation: The Kadambas (4th century CE, Banavasi in Uttara Kannada) are regarded as the first indigenous Kannada-speaking dynasty.

questions.question: Talakadu, on the banks of the Kaveri, was the capital of which dynasty?
questions.explanation: The Western Ganga dynasty ruled from Talakadu (near Mysuru) from the 4th to 11th centuries; the town is famed for its buried temples.

questions.question: The magnificent Kailasa (Kailashnath) temple at Ellora was carved by which Rashtrakuta ruler?
questions.explanation: Krishna I (8th century) commissioned the Kailasa temple — the world's largest monolithic rock-cut structure, carved top-down from a single rock.

questions.question: Which Chalukya king of Badami defeated Emperor Harshavardhana on the banks of the Narmada?
questions.explanation: Pulakeshin II (610–642 CE) halted Harsha's southward expansion on the Narmada; the Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang praised his reign.

questions.question: The royal emblem of the Hoysalas depicts what?
questions.explanation: The Hoysala crest shows the founder Sala striking a tiger — 'Hoy Sala' ('strike, Sala') — found on all their temples.

questions.question: Basavanna, the 12th-century philosopher and social reformer, established which spiritual parliament of the Sharana movement?
questions.explanation: Basavanna's Anubhava Mantapa at Kalyana was an early 'parliament' of mystics and reformers; their sayings form the Vachana literature.

questions.question: The Vachana Sahitya, revolutionary Kannada prose-poems, is associated with which movement?
options: The Bhakti movement of Purandara Dasa
questions.explanation: Vachanas are short poetic sayings of the 12th-century Sharana movement — Basavanna, Akka Mahadevi, Allama Prabhu.

questions.question: The Mysuru Dasara celebrations were started in 1610 by which Wodeyar ruler?
questions.explanation: Raja Wodeyar I began the grand Dasara (Nadahabba) at Srirangapatna in 1610, later continued at Mysuru.

questions.question: What are the colours of the widely used Kannada flag?
questions.explanation: The Kannada flag has yellow (top, for arishina/turmeric) and red (bottom, for kumkuma); it is an unofficial but popular emblem of the state.

questions.question: According to folklore, Bengaluru's name derives from which Kannada phrase?
options: Benda Kaalu Ooru (town of boiled beans)
Bili Kallu Ooru (town of white stones)
questions.explanation: Legend says a Hoysala king was fed boiled beans (benda kaalu) by an old woman, naming the settlement after the meal.

questions.question: Where is the headquarters of ISRO?
questions.explanation: ISRO's headquarters is at Antariksh Bhavan, Bengaluru; its launch site is Sriharikota and VSSC is at Thiruvananthapuram.

questions.question: Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL), India's aerospace major, is headquartered in which city?
questions.explanation: HAL, founded in 1940 as Hindustan Aircraft Company, is headquartered in Bengaluru — the maker of the Tejas fighter.

questions.question: Infosys, the Bengaluru-headquartered IT giant, was co-founded in 1981 by whom?
questions.explanation: Narayana Murthy and six colleagues founded Infosys with ₹10,000; Azim Premji led Wipro and Shiv Nadar founded HCL.

questions.question: Channapatna, famous for its GI-tagged lacquerware wooden toys, lies in which district?
questions.explanation: Channapatna's wooden toys trace their craft to Tipu Sultan's era; the craft got a GI tag in 2005.

questions.question: Mysore Pak, the famous sweet, is traditionally credited to which royal kitchen?
options: The Mysuru palace kitchen of Kakasura Madappa
questions.explanation: Chef Kakasura Madappa is said to have created Mysore Pak in the palace kitchens during Krishnaraja Wodeyar's reign (early 1930s).

questions.question: What was the first Kannada talkie film, released in 1934?
questions.explanation: Sati Sulochana (1934), starring Subbaiah Naidu and directed by Y. V. Rao, was the first Kannada film with sound.
